entities.name: Abraham of Arbela
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abraham of Arbela (died c. 344 CE) was a bishop of Arbela (modern Erbil in Iraqi Kurdistan) who was martyred during the Great Persecution of Christians under the Sassanid Persian Shah Shapur II. He is venerated as a martyr in the Eastern Church traditions, particularly in the Church of the East (Assyrian), which traces its origins to Mesopotamian Christian communities.

Shapur II (309–379) conducted systematic persecutions of Persian Christians, partly motivated by Rome's conversion under Constantine, which made Persian Christians suspect as potential Roman fifth-columnists. Abraham of Arbela was among thousands of Christians executed during these persecutions, which are collectively commemorated in the Church of the East's martyrology. Arbela (Erbil) was one of the most important Christian cities of the Persian Empire, with a Christian community stretching back to the first century.

His martyrdom placed him within the extraordinary tradition of Mesopotamian Christian martyrdom under Persian rule — a tradition that shaped the Church of the East's identity as a suffering community, distinct from both the Roman imperial Church and the Zoroastrian Persian establishment. The martyrology of the Persian Church represents one of the largest bodies of early Christian martyr tradition outside the Roman world.
